paper_metadata.title: Effect of the valence electron concentration on the yield strength of Ti–Zr–Nb–V high-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: Effect of the valence electron concentration on the yield strength of Ti–Zr–Nb–V high-entropy alloys
The as-cast Ti–Zr–Nb–V alloy ingots was prepared by vacuum arc melting from raw metals with a purity of > 99.9% in a high-purity argon atmosphere.
The ingot was remelted at least 6 times to achieve a homogeneous distribution of the constituent elements.
The samples used for the subsequent characterization measurements were cut from the ingot by electrical discharge machining.
It is observed that all of the alloys have one set of sharp diffraction peaks that belong to a BCC structure.

From the TEM-SAED images (Fig. 4), it is confirmed that the precipitations at the boundaries between the BCC solid solution contain a small amount of the V2Zr Laves phase that cannot be detected by XRD.
It is observed that the V15, V20 and V21.3 alloys present the typical dendrites.
It is interesting that in the alloys consisting of less V, including V15, V20 and V21.3, there are some fine grains featuring a size below 100 µm. These fine grains arrange into chains.
It is well-known that the dendritic structure always includes some casting defects such as shrinkage cavities.

It is observed that V25 displays the best performance with excellent values for the yield strength (σy) and elongation of 876 MPa and 20.7% (the strain was not directly measured by extensometry), respectively.

It is a meaningful scientific question whether it is possible to intrinsically improve the performance of alloys, in other words, by adjusting the cohesive energy of the solid-solution lattice itself without giving rise to new structures.

conflicts.description: The reported compression yield strength of V30 and V35 contradicts the stated increase of yield strength with increasing V/Zr ratio, as V30 and V35 have the same value of 1010 MPa.

The text states that the yield strength of Ti–Zr–Nb–V alloys increases with increasing V/Zr ratio, but the compression data shows a slight decrease from V25 (969 MPa) to V30 (1010 MPa) and V35 (1010 MPa) remains same as V30.

claim_1.property: yield strength increases with V/Zr ratio

evidence.quote: It is observed that with the exception of the brittle V35 alloy, the values of both σy and σu of the Ti–Zr–Nb–V alloys increase with increasing V/Zr ratios, while εf remains stable at a very high level of approximately 40–45% compared with the reported RHEAs.
